---
title: "Explore the taxonomic hierarchy"
format: html
---

Here we present a practical guide to the `funga_get_children_taxa()` function of the `fungaR` package. It retrieves all child taxa — species, subspecies, varieties, and so on — below a given taxonomic name and rank, which is useful for getting every species in a genus, every genus in an order, and similar hierarchy traversals.

## Function Overview

`funga_get_children_taxa()` first locates the parent taxon in the [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) checklist, then returns every taxon whose lineage includes that parent's taxon ID. Fungi are classified in FFB by Division (phylum-equivalent, e.g. Ascomycota, Basidiomycota) rather than Class, and FFB does not register a standalone family-rank taxon record for Fungi — `rank = "family"` is still supported, but matched directly against the `family` classification column on genus/species records instead of walking a family-rank row.

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `taxon_name` | Character. Scientific name to search for (e.g. `"Trichoderma"`, `"Xylariaceae"`, `"Agaricales"`). |
| `rank` | Character. Taxonomic rank of `taxon_name`: `"division"`, `"order"`, `"family"`, `"genus"`, or `"species"`. Default `"genus"`. |
| `child_rank` | Character or `NULL`. Rank(s) to return as children. `NULL` (default) returns **all** descendant ranks; a single rank (e.g. `"species"`) restricts the result to that rank only. Requesting `child_rank = "family"` from a division/order returns a *derived* summary (family name, order, and genus count) rather than real FFB rows, since none exist for Fungi. |
| `include_synonyms` | Logical. If `TRUE`, includes synonym names in addition to accepted ones. Default `FALSE`. |
| `version` | FFB dataset version to use. Defaults to `"latest"`. |
| `rm_funga_database` | If `TRUE`, deletes the cached database after the search. Default `FALSE` is recommended for repeated use. |
| `verbose` | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), prints progress messages. |

## Get all species in a genus

```r
library(fungaR)

species <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Trichoderma",
                                   rank = "genus",
                                   child_rank = "species")
```

## Get every descendant of a genus

Species, subspecies, and varieties together:

```r
all_descendants <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Trichoderma",
                                           rank = "genus",
                                           child_rank = NULL)
```

## Get all genera in a family, including synonyms

Matched via the `family` classification column, since FFB has no family-rank row for Fungi:

```r
genera <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Xylariaceae",
                                  rank = "family",
                                  child_rank = "genus",
                                  include_synonyms = TRUE)
```

## Get all genera in an order

```r
genera_in_order <- funga_get_children_taxa(taxon_name = "Agaricales",
                                            rank = "order",
                                            child_rank = "genus")
```

## Additional Tips

- Set `child_rank = NULL` when you want a complete picture of a group's diversity, including infraspecific taxa; set it to a single rank (e.g. `"species"`) when you specifically need a species-level checklist for downstream work.
- `rank` must correctly describe `taxon_name` (e.g. don't pass a genus name with `rank = "order"`) — the function looks up the parent by matching both together.
- Combine with [`funga_records()`](/articles/filter_ffb_records.qmd) when you need geographic or trait filters in addition to hierarchy traversal (e.g. all species in a genus that are also endemic to a given state).
